ai.title: Surface agent validation transport errors in CLI chat
ai.summary: Agent validation transport failures now block message sending and display the specific error reason in the CLI chat instead of silently aborting with an empty error list. The useAgentValidation hook no longer filters out network errors, and the sendMessage hook elevates validation failures from warnings to error-level telemetry while injecting a descriptive error message into the chat transcript. The SDK validation layer includes the HTTP status code in remote error messages for clearer diagnostics.
ai.evidence: In cli/src/hooks/use-agent-validation.ts, the validate callback now assigns validationResult.validationErrors directly to state instead of filtering them, and returns a constructed error object in the catch block. In cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts, the validation failure block replaces a logger.warn call with logger.error and injects a createErrorChatMessage containing the first error's message into the chat history. In sdk/src/validate-agents.ts, the remote validation error message format changed to include the HTTP status code explicitly.

entries.title: SDK update: windows-bash
entries.summary: SDK changes across 1 file(s) (+20/−3).

ai.title: SDK checks FREEBUFF GIT DIR for bundled Git and bash
ai.summary: The SDK's Windows shell resolution now checks the `FREEBUFF_GIT_DIR` environment variable before searching standard install locations and PATH. In `windowsBashCandidates`, a candidate path is constructed by joining `FREEBUFF_GIT_DIR` with `bin` and `bash.exe`. Similarly, `windowsGitCandidates` appends a candidate by joining `FREEBUFF_GIT_DIR` with `cmd` and `git.exe`, positioned after GitHub Desktop's bundled Git. This mechanism allows the packaged Desktop application to supply its own Git for Windows installation without requiring a system install or global PATH change.
ai.evidence: sdk/src/tools/windows-bash.ts adds `env.FREEBUFF_GIT_DIR` to `windowsBashCandidates` and `windowsGitCandidates`, and sdk/src/__tests__/windows-bash.test.ts adds tests verifying that `findWindowsBash` uses the app bundle and falls back to installed Git.

eli5.text: The desktop app can now supply its own version of the command-line tools needed to run code on Windows, without requiring a separate system-wide installation. This helps anyone using the desktop application on a fresh computer where those tools are not yet installed globally. In daily use, you may see the assistant successfully run terminal commands on Windows machines where it previously could not find the required tools, though no action is needed to enable this.

ai.title: Add starter templates, agent scope rules, and Sites publication checks
ai.summary: This commit introduces a starter template subsystem in the common package, adding agent tools to list and apply pre-built project scaffolds and a shared catalogue schema for fetching templates from a public R2 bucket. The base3 agent prompt is updated to enforce scope discipline, requiring the agent to size work to the request and verify changes in proportion to their impact rather than running full test suites for small edits. Sites publishing logic now distinguishes between deployment and publication, adding an isPublished check and specific error recovery instructions for published site limits and saved project limits.
ai.evidence: New files `common/src/templates/catalog.ts`, `common/src/templates/tools.ts`, and `common/src/templates/guidance.ts` define the starter template system, including `template_list` and `template_apply` agent tools, a public catalogue fetcher, and standing prompt guidance. Modifications in `agents/base3.ts` add scope-discipline and proportional-verification rules to the agent system prompt, while `common/src/sites/publish.ts` introduces publication-status checks and distinct recovery instructions for site limits.

Updated base3 agent system prompt to include scope discipline and proportional verification rules.

Integrated template analytics into desktop and product funnel schemas and updated Cloud history project types.

eli5.text: The AI coding assistant now has access to a new library of ready-made project starters, allowing it to quickly set up common apps like dashboards or online stores in an empty workspace. The assistant's instructions were also updated to match its effort to your specific request, meaning it will skip heavy planning and testing for small fixes but perform thorough checks for larger changes. Additionally, the system now clearly distinguishes between uploading code and actually publishing a website, ensuring you know if a site is truly live even if a previous step was paused. This makes starting new projects faster and gives you more predictable, proportionate results from the assistant.

ai.title: Hide session clock on untimed models
ai.summary: A new `untimedModelIds` field added to the `FreebuffFreebucksInfo` wire type allows the server to designate specific models where the session clock, countdown, and hour-end notices should be hidden from the user. The `StatusBar` component in the CLI now checks this server verdict via the `freebuffSessionUntimed` utility; when the active model is marked untimed, the draining progress bar and numeric remaining-time readout are suppressed. This change is paired with the `spendWithoutAsking` flag, which allows these untimed hours to renew silently on the next send without user interaction.
ai.evidence: The `freebuffSessionUntimed` function in `common/src/util/freebuff-model-selection.ts` returns true when the session's `model` appears in the `untimedModelIds` array of `FreebuffFreebucksInfo`; the `StatusBar` component in `cli/src/components/status-bar.tsx` uses this function to nullify the `clock` variable, suppressing the session progress bar and countdown text when the model is marked untimed by the server.
ai.unknowns: The specific business rule determining which models are marked untimed (e.g., the exact tier or hour-duration thresholds) is not visible in the diff, only the resulting wire field.

changes.what: Added `untimedModelIds` optional field to the `FreebuffFreebucksInfo` interface to carry the server's verdict on which models hide their session clock.
Implemented the `freebuffSessionUntimed` utility function that checks if a given model ID is present in the `untimedModelIds` array of a Freebucks info object.

Updated `StatusBar` to use the `freebuffSessionUntimed` check, replacing the direct `sessionProgress` reference with a `clock` variable that becomes null when the model is untimed, thereby hiding the progress bar and countdown text.

eli5.text: For some accounts using the free tier, the timer and countdown that track your remaining session time will no longer appear on certain models when the service provider says so. This applies specifically to users with full access on paid tiers who are running short sessions, where the next hour automatically renews without asking for confirmation. You will see a cleaner interface with no time warnings or progress bars draining on those specific models, while everyone else continues to see the clock as before.

This ensures that when you open your project again, the tool recognizes your previous conversation history instead of starting fresh. As a result, your chat history and context are preserved across sessions when working on hosted websites.
